Meter for the highlights. Shadows can be lifted in the Develop Lab; blown highlights are gone forever. Expose for what you cannot recover.
Today's assignment: one subject, ten frames, no two from the same distance. Post the one that surprises you.
The histogram is a weather report, not a grade. A scene with true blacks and true whites should use the whole graph — a tidy centered histogram of a night street is usually a wrong exposure.
Transmission prompt: photograph something that is ending — last light, last bite, a closing door. No people required; the feeling is the subject.
Focus on the near eye. In any portrait, the eye closest to the lens carries the frame; if it drifts soft, the whole image feels like a mistake.
Today's assignment: shoot only shadows for one hour. The objects casting them stay out of frame.
Your feet are a zoom lens with better perspective. Two steps forward changes the story more than a focal length ever will.
Transmission prompt: find the oldest thing on your street and photograph it like it is new.
Shoot the moment before the moment. The breath before the note, the step before the leap — anticipation is where the honest frames live.
Today's assignment: a portrait at f/1.8 and the same portrait at f/8. Study what the background does to the story in each.
Check your edges before your subject. Poles from heads, bright corners, stray hands — frames are lost at their borders more often than at their centers.
Transmission prompt: color discipline — spend one walk shooting only frames where green appears exactly once.
ISO is not the enemy. A sharp frame at ISO 6400 beats a blurred one at ISO 100 every night of the week. Noise is texture; blur is failure.
Today's assignment: slow shutter, steady hands. Drag a moving subject at 1/15 and keep one element tack sharp.
One light, mastered, beats three lights guessed. Move a single source around your subject for a week and you will learn more than any diagram teaches.
Transmission prompt: photograph your morning as if it belonged to a stranger. What would they learn about you?
The reciprocal rule is a floor, not a target: one over your focal length keeps you safe. For critical sharpness, double it.
Today's assignment: three frames of the same corner at three different hours. Light is the only variable.
Chimp with intent: after each frame, name one thing you would change. If you cannot name one, you are documenting, not photographing.
Transmission prompt: get low. Every frame today from below knee height — the world is taller than your habits.
White balance is a creative decision wearing a technical costume. Set it for the light you want the viewer to feel, not the light that happened to be there.
Today's assignment: shoot a stranger's hands at work — ask first, or keep them anonymous. Hands confess what faces hide.
Backgrounds are chosen, not found. Before you press, ask what your subject is standing in front of — then move until the answer is: nothing that argues.
Transmission prompt: one frame, one word — wait. Find the scene on your street that is holding its breath.
Learn your metering modes like gears in a car: matrix for the highway, spot for the mountain road. The wrong mode in the wrong place is a stall.
Today's assignment: fill the frame until the subject has nowhere to hide. Then take one more step in.
Shoot a series, not a single. The second and third frames of the same idea are where accidents turn into style.
Transmission prompt: photograph the sound of your neighborhood. If the frame hums, you have it.
